withdraw.missing: a formula-surface reading of the facing attribute of sig.warning_lamp (e.g. sig_warning_lamp [x, colour, mode, facing], or a selector sig_warning_lamp_facing [x, facing]). Span u4, together with the words that the definition reference u5 borrows from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3 ('at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'), is a condition on when the duty arises. It decides which road users the duty concerns and when it arises: the approaching authorized emergency vehicle or regulatory-agency vehicle triggers the duty only while it shows a flashing red lamp that is visible from the front. The ontology's contract gives sig.warning_lamp a facing attribute in {front, rear, side}, but Core's evaluator only reads the atom by colour and mode, so the rule can only state 'a red flashing warning lamp lit, in any facing'. That fact is weaker than the condition, because a vehicle that shows a flashing red lamp only to the rear or side would also trigger the duty. Rule 3 says a condition is never narrowed or weakened, and no other atom carries the lamp's facing, so the span is withdrawn until Core exposes the facing selector. Once it does, the record as planned (colour red, mode flashing, facing front) codes as is: the coder's run 2 passed the gate with every other element written.
nearest: sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing ∈ {front, rear, side}': the contract carries facing, but the formula surface reads only colour and mode (sig_warning_lamp [x, colour] / [x, colour, mode]), so 'visible from the front' cannot be stated

rel.visible: 'b is visible from a ... Not a stand-in for: ... a lamp being lit — a visible vehicle may show no lamp and a lit lamp may be hidden': it relates two road users' bodies, not the direction a lamp faces
rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame': it places the subject ahead of the approaching vehicle (already used for u1), but it says nothing about which way the vehicle's lamp faces
